appraisal_events.evidence: « un des grands tralalas de ma tante, puisque tante il y a », says Gilberte « d'un air fin », affecting disdain for « cette tante mauvais teint »; she « se considérait comme une Guermantes de tout temps » and as touched by her uncle's misalliance, « tandis que, naturellement, ce n'était que hors de sa présence qu'on avait parlé de la mésalliance qu'avait faite Saint-Loup en l'épousant ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte snubs the parvenue aunt as an intruder into the family, and the narration turns the snub back on her by recalling that her own marriage was the misalliance the family mocked behind her back.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Les nouvelles générations en concluaient que la duchesse de Guermantes, malgré son nom, devait être quelque demi-castor qui n'avait jamais été tout à fait du gratin »; the new strata, misreading her royal protocol, conclude « que la position de la duchesse était d'autant plus basse », and her first situation in Paris is said to exist only « dans les esprits qui y croient ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Society's newer voices are shown revising the duchesse downward: her intimacy with an actress and her withdrawal from the faubourg are read as proof that she never quite belonged, and the narrator confirms that her supremacy now depends on belief alone.

appraisal_events.evidence: Rachel, « devenue une actrice célèbre », is in intimate conversation with the duchesse and recites at the matinée; « la nouvelle avait couru dans Paris que les invitations étaient au nom de la princesse de Guermantes, mais que c'était Rachel qui, en réalité, recevait chez la princesse » — she who « avait reçu jadis sa plus terrible avanie » from Mme de Guermantes.
appraisal_events.explanation: The former kept woman is now the courted friend of the duchesse and the drawing card of a Guermantes matinée, and Paris says she is its real hostess. The narration ironizes the rise by first showing her, unrecognized, as « une affreuse vieille femme ».

appraisal_events.evidence: For the tea she gives for her son and daughter-in-law « les invités ne se pressaient pas d'arriver »; Bloch answers « Non, j'aime mieux aller chez la princesse de Guermantes », and « c'est ce qu'au fond de soi chacun avait décidé »; at her house « il y avait vide absolu et mort », and the meal is eaten « comme pour un repas funéraire », the single young guest leaving in turn for the Guermantes.
appraisal_events.explanation: Her own faithful desert her in a body for the rival gathering, and the passage stages the empty room as the measure of her eclipse by the Rachel she still calls a « grue ».

status_effects.explanation: She comes off worse for a pretension the narrator immediately deflates: the self-styled Guermantes of all time is the one the family had mocked for a misalliance.
Her standing is spoken of as fallen by the generation now doing the ranking, which takes her for someone who was never quite of the gratin.
Paris itself reports her as the real hostess of a Guermantes matinée and the duchesse's chosen friend; her local standing rises sharply.
The Guermantes threshold that once expelled her — it was at Mme de Guermantes's that she suffered « sa plus terrible avanie » — now admits her to the platform of the princesse's own party.
The gathering she convened is emptied by another interior: everyone crosses into the Guermantes party and she is left outside it, at a table set for absent guests.
The desertion is a public verdict on her standing: her most faithful admirers weigh her against Rachel's afternoon and choose Rachel, without a word of excuse.

ambiguities: In this chapter « princesse de Guermantes » is shared between Marie-Gilbert and the new princesse; here the hostess is the former Mme Verdurin, whom the passage names outright (« la mésalliance que son oncle avait faite en épousant Mme Verdurin »), so the surface form is resolved to that entity.

Rachel's social rise coexists with a brutal physical diminishment — the narrator at first sees only « une affreuse vieille femme », « cette immonde vieille » — which this annotation does not record as a separate status movement.
